title: Kinetics of central macular thickness reduction in patients with macular edema after intravitreal drug therapy

license.statement: Open access permitting unrestricted noncommercial use with citation (article <license>; publisher licence, no Creative Commons URL)

condition: Macular edema secondary to diabetic retinopathy (5 eyes) or retinal vein occlusion (3 central, 1 branch), 9 patients, Stanford, November-December 2008; prospective observational kinetics study; agent chosen by the treating physician; all eyes had previously received intravitreal injections; one study eye per patient

notes: Measure: Methods state that the software-generated central subfield mean thickness was recorded as central macular thickness (Cirrus HD-OCT 512 x 128 macular cube): central_subfield, device cirrus.

Table 1 footnote states baseline values are from SD-OCT; the 48-hour and 1-week columns carry no instrument label; their column means agree with the SD-OCT entries of Table 3, so the Cirrus SD-OCT device is recorded for all three columns.
Times: 48 hours = 48/730.5 months, 1 week = 7/30.4375 months, both counted from the single injection.
Kind individual: Table 1 gives one row per treated eye; groups are formed by diagnosis and agent as reported per patient.
Two of 91 SD-OCT scans had segmentation corrected manually (Methods).
